summary: Iteration 4 tested end-to-end. 20/20 new backend tests (legal + admin config + webp) PASS. 82/83 regression pass (1 pre-existing flaky brute-force test under xdist parallel). Frontend verified: TrustBand fully removed, home scrollHeight=2278px @1440x900 (well under 3200), 10/10 asset images are .webp, Shop nav (testid=header-nav-shop) smooth-scrolls to #products, footer Customer Care has all 5 legal SPA links, Admin /admin/config lists 27 files (including 12 nested legal/*), editor loads/saves/shows inline invalid-JSON error. Fixed 1 bug in LegalPage.jsx where all 5 legal routes rendered 'Terms & Conditions' because routes are static (no :slug param) — added useLocation fallback so each route resolves to its own document.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED by testing agent — useParams().slug is undefined for static routes /terms-and-conditions etc., so LegalPage always fell back to 'terms_and_conditions' and rendered the same doc for ALL 5 legal routes. Fix: derive slug from useLocation().pathname when useParams slug is absent. Verified: after fix, /privacy-policy shows 'Privacy Policy' H1, /returns-refunds shows 'Returns & Refund Policy', /shipping-delivery shows 'Shipping & Delivery Policy', /payment-policy shows 'Payment Policy'.

action_items: Main agent: review LegalPage.jsx fix (added useLocation fallback for slug derivation). Consider migrating routes to use path parameter (/legal/:slug) or keep current static routes with useLocation fallback.

Optional: test_admin_api.py::test_bruteforce_lockout is flaky when pytest-xdist runs in parallel — parallel workers race on the lockout counter. Not related to iteration 4. Consider marking with @pytest.mark.serial or resetting db.admin_login_attempts inside the test.
critical_code_review_comments: LegalPage.jsx used useParams().slug but App.js uses static routes (/terms-and-conditions) with no :slug param — a design mismatch that made 4 of 5 legal pages silently identical. Testing agent fixed with useLocation fallback. Ideal fix: define a single dynamic route /:legalSlug or /legal/:slug and add a slug allow-list guard.

admin_config.py._resolve uses 'CONFIG_DIR.resolve() not in target.parents' which correctly blocks '../server.py' (returns 400), verified by test. However it allows any nested folder that happens to be inside CONFIG_DIR — currently only legal/ exists so this is safe.
server.py legal_document endpoint injects manifest metadata AFTER json load — if json file has its own 'title', it wins (setdefault). Good pattern.
AdminConfigFilesPage editor uses a plain textarea (no syntax highlighting). Acceptable for admin usage but consider Monaco for larger JSONs.

Footer.customerCare labels/urls in config are hard-coded 'Track Your Order' → /account (correct) but the customerCare list mixes legal (5 entries) with account (1 entry). Consider splitting into 'Legal' + 'Support' for clarity.
